newsitem.title: GERMANY: German millers see lack of top quality wheat.
newsitem.headline: German millers see lack of top quality wheat.

text.p: A lack of top quality grain should boost German bread wheat prices in the fourth quarter of 1997, the ADH millers association said on Thursday.
"Wheat yields and volumes will be very good this year but there is relatively less high quality wheat that is essential to millers," an ADH official said in a telephone interview.
"This means we will have to be pay premiums for the high qualities and this will increase overall costs."
Millers were paying 272.50-287.50 marks/tonne free mill for new crop standard bread wheat of 12.5-13 percent protein and 220-250 hagberg, 20-30 marks above prices last year.
But the exceptional qualities needed for blending with around 14.0-14.5 percent protein and falling numbers above 300 were either unavailable or cost 340 marks, 40-50 marks more than a year ago.
"The market for that segment has not developed as farmers store the high qualities away," the ADH source said.
"Britain had a large wheat crop but qualities are not great and they might have to import top grades."
"France started out with unusually high 12.5 percent protein but latest qualities look mediocre."

Bonn farm ministry estimates are for a 2.7 percent higher wheat crop at 18.42 million tonnes, with yields at 7.09 tonnes per hectare (6.89 in 1995) from a 0.7 percent higher area of 2.59 million hectares.
Farmers planted more quality wheat but changeable weather throughout the year resulted in variable quality.
ADH expects average protein contents around one percent down from last year's 12.5 percent on average.
An official quality assessment is due only at the end of the month because of harvest delays well into the middle of September and quality variations.
Current German FOB wheat prices are in a 280-320 marks range in Baltic ports.
Brokers think the market has peaked as France's record 34 million wheat crop should undermine European prices, depending on the amount of third country exports that are authorised.
